walkthroughs.body_html:
Hot deserts sit near 30 degrees latitude.

The Sahara covers ~9 million km2 of North Africa.

Receives less than 250 mm of rain a year.

Savannah has two seasons.

The Serengeti in Tanzania hosts the famous wildebeest migration.

Drought-resistant grasses dominate.

Tundra wraps the high Arctic.

Permafrost lies under thin active soil; growing season is under 3 months.

It is fragile and vulnerable to climate change.

options: Tundra
Savannah
Taiga
Hot desert

mcqs.q: Permafrost is a key feature of which biome?
options: Tropical rainforest
Tundra
Hot desert
Deciduous forest

mcqs.q: What is the difference between the tundra and the taiga biomes?
options: Hurricanes form when two cold fronts collide above the ocean.
Tundra is treeless cold biome (too cold and permafrost-dominated for trees), while taiga (boreal forest) is the band of coniferous forest just south of the tundra in subarctic latitudes.
Tundra is in the Arctic and taiga is in the Antarctic.
Tundra and taiga are the same biome with different names.

mcqs.q: Why are tropical rainforest soils typically infertile?
options: Heavy rainfall leaches nutrients, and most nutrients are stored in living biomass and rapidly recycled — the soil itself holds very little.
Because so much vegetation grows there, the soil must be fertile.
Because rainforest soils are made of clay.
Tundra is in the Arctic and taiga is in the Antarctic.

mcqs.q: Why do tropical cyclones only form over warm tropical oceans?
options: Hurricanes form wherever there are strong winds over the sea.
Because rainforest soils are made of clay.
They need sea surface temperatures above ~27 degrees C to a depth of 50m to provide energy through evaporation, plus enough Coriolis effect (away from the equator) to spin.
Hurricanes form when two cold fronts collide above the ocean.
